topic.angle: Squares A and B are the same shade

card.title: Are A and B the same shade?

body.question: A checkerboard with light and dark squares is partly shadowed by another object. Square A looks darker than square B. In the image itself, how do they compare?
body.reveal: Within the context of the two-dimensional image, A and B are of identical brightness: they would be printed with identical mixtures of ink, or displayed on a screen with pixels of identical color. Edward H. Adelson, professor of vision science at MIT, published the illusion in 1995. It demonstrates the context-dependent nature of human color perception.

probes.question: True or false: in the checker shadow illusion, areas A and B would be printed with identical mixtures of ink.
In what year was the checker shadow illusion published?
